card.title: 5e CHASSEURS

card.flavorText: The 5th Foot Rifle Battalion is a unit of the French Army created in 1840. They became famous for participating in some of the harshest battles which took place during the early years of the Great War, in the Vosges mountains, notably on the Linge battlefield in 1915. It was renamed 5th Motorized Rifle Battalion in 1937 and became part of the 1st Armored Division when it was created in January 1940, joining 4 tanks battalions and one artillery regiment. This was the largest and most powerful unit in the French Army when the war broke out, but it lacked training, having only recently been formed. During the Battle of France, the Division first joined the French 9th Army in Belgium in May 1940, facing the 7. and 9. Panzerdivision. They suffered heavy casualties and had to be reformed at the end of the month. They kept fighting after the Germans invaded France, but ultimately faced the same difficulties plaguing the whole French Army at the time: late orders, poor fuel supply, lack of anti-aircraft support and communication issues. It was disbanded after the fall of France in June 1940. In 1945, during the liberation of France, around 200 members of the maquis reformed the unit within the French Forces of the Interior. They participated in the liberation of Vieux-Thann in Alsace, and then moved to Redon, Brittany, to take part in the siege of the Saint-Nazaire pocket, where 30,000 Germans soldiers resisted until May 1945.
